scope: Immutable source and standards review. No new connection, provider request, router, network, security or limit change. Does not diagnose the particular router or prove a new route.
findings: Browser requests iceTransportPolicy all, but both clients enforce a narrower public IPv4 srflx and reviewed TURN policy. Private, host, mDNS and IPv6 paths are not usable production candidates.
Native production ICETransportPolicyNoHost, public remote-IP filter and long peer-reflexive acceptance wait reinforce that boundary. The test-only lab path is not a production LAN mode.

Same Wi-Fi or Ethernet does not promise direct private-LAN audio. The recorded relay/srflx pairs are compatible with this policy. A failed public direct route may involve NAT hairpinning or another topology factor; the exact cause is not established.

Both endpoints obtain normal issuer credentials before negotiation. Direct selection does not bypass issuer admission or its operation, rate and monthly-usage checks. Mint/mailbox operation counters and actual TURN ingress/egress are different measurements; a daily operation cap is not necessarily exhausted media bandwidth.
Browser transport-byte and credential-TTL limits apply even when a public direct pair is selected. These safety/session limits do not directly measure billed TURN egress.

No port forwarding, lab mode, private-address expansion, quota reset or provider activation is proposed. Any trusted-LAN or staged STUN/TURN design needs a separate compatibility and security review; it is not implemented by this note.
